items.contents:
Math functions

FunctionArgumentsUse
Math.lerp(a, b, t)Interpolate between two values.
Math.clamp(value, min, max)Keep a value inside a range.
Math.map(value, inMin, inMax, outMin, outMax)Convert one range to another.
Math.moveTowards(current, target, maxDelta)Move toward a target.
Math.smoothstep(a, b, t)Smoothly interpolate.
Math.wrap(value, min, max)Wrap a value into a range.
Math.degToRad(degrees)Convert degrees to radians.
Math.radToDeg(radians)Convert radians to degrees.
Math.distance(a, b)Distance between two 2D vectors.
Math.randInt(min, max)Random whole number from min through max.

items.subtitle: Common JavaScript math
items.contents:
Common Math functions

You can also use standard JavaScript Math functions supported by the expression field, such as Math.abs, Math.floor, Math.ceil, Math.round, Math.sqrt, Math.pow, Math.sin, Math.cos, Math.tan, Math.atan2, Math.min, and Math.max.

items.subtitle: Vectors
items.contents:
Vectors

FunctionArgumentsUse
vec2(x, y)Create a 2D vector.
length(v)Get vector length.
dot(a, b)Get the dot product.
normalize(v)Turn a vector into a unit direction.

items.subtitle: Function argument hints
items.contents:
Function argument hints

The Expression Library shows function names together with their argument names, such as Math.randInt(min, max), so you can see what values the function expects before using it.

items.subtitle: Microphone expressions
items.contents:
Microphone expressions

When microphone use is enabled and permission is available, the Expression Library provides a Mic group.

ExpressionMeaning
ctx.mic.decibelCurrent microphone loudness level.
ctx.mic.speechCurrent speech-recognition text while recognition is active.
ctx.mic.activeWhether microphone input is currently active.
ctx.mic.speechActiveWhether speech recognition is currently running.

These values are intended for runtime expressions, such as showing a live microphone meter, reacting to a sound level, or displaying recognized speech.

items.subtitle: Misc — color helper functions
items.contents:
Misc — Color helper functions

The Expression Library has a Misc group for small utility helpers that do not belong to Variables, Input, Math, or Vectors.

ExpressionResult
ctx.col.rgb(r, g, b)Returns a #RRGGBB hex color. r, g, and b use 0–255.
ctx.col.rgba(r, g, b, a)Returns a #RRGGBBAA hex color. r, g, and b use 0–255. Alpha accepts 0–1 or 0–255.
ctx.col.rgb(255, 128, 0)
ctx.col.rgba(255, 128, 0, 0.5)

The helpers are available to expressions in the editor and runtime.

items.subtitle: JavaScript values and operators
items.contents:
JavaScript values and operators

Expression fields use JavaScript-style expressions for calculations and conditions. The basic pieces you will use most often are numbers, strings, booleans, properties, arithmetic, comparisons, and logical operators.

SyntaxExampleMeaning
Arithmetic10 + 5 * 2Calculate numbers.
Comparisonctx.global.score >= 100Check a condition.
Equalityctx.local.state === "dead"Check whether two values are equal.
Not equalctx.local.health !== 0Check whether values differ.
ANDa && bBoth conditions must be true.
ORa || bAt least one condition must be true.
NOT!ctx.local.deadReverse a boolean value.

items.subtitle: Ternary operator
items.contents:
Ternary operator

The ternary operator chooses one of two values using a condition:

condition ? truth : falsy

For example:

ctx.global.score >= 100 ? "Winner" : "Keep Playing"

If the condition is true, the expression produces "Winner". Otherwise it produces "Keep Playing".

This is useful when an input needs one value for one case and another value for the opposite case.

items.subtitle: Optional chaining
items.contents:
Optional chaining ?.

Optional chaining lets you safely read a property when an earlier value might not exist.

ctx.node?.name

Without optional chaining, trying to read a property from a missing value can cause an error. With ?., the result becomes undefined instead of stopping the expression at that point.

It can also be used through a chain:

ctx.node?.sprite?.src

Use it when an object or Component may be absent.

items.subtitle: Nullish coalescing
items.contents:
Nullish coalescing ??

?? supplies a fallback when the value on its left is null or undefined.

ctx.local.name ?? "Player"

If ctx.local.name has a real value, that value is used. If it is missing, "Player" is used instead.

This is different from using || when you need to keep valid values such as 0 or false.

items.subtitle: Property and bracket access
items.contents:
Property and bracket access

Use a dot to read a normal property:

ctx.position.x
ctx.global.score

Use brackets when the property name is dynamic or is not a convenient identifier:

ctx.events.key["1"]
ctx.local["player-name"]

Bracket access is also useful when a value comes from another expression.

items.subtitle: Parentheses and order
items.contents:
Parentheses and order

Parentheses let you make the intended order of a calculation explicit.

(ctx.global.score + 10) * 2

Without parentheses, multiplication is evaluated before addition. Use parentheses whenever a long expression could be confusing or when a comparison is combined with several logical operators.

items.subtitle: Operators quick reference
items.contents:
Operators quick reference

The Expression Library includes common operators you can insert into an expression.

OperatorMeaning
&&Logical AND
||Logical OR
<, >Less than / greater than
<=, >=Less than or equal / greater than or equal
==Loose equality
===Strict equality
+, -, *, /Arithmetic operators
(condition) ? true : falseTernary conditional expression

The inserted operator is only a starting point; edit the expression to supply operands and values.

items.subtitle: Timing and conversion helpers
items.contents:
Timing and conversion helpers

performance.now() is a high-resolution elapsed-time value in milliseconds and is useful for measuring durations and profiling. Date.now() returns the current Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

Useful conversion helpers include Number(value), String(value), Boolean(value), parseInt(value), parseFloat(value), and isNaN(value). ctx.isVisible reports whether the current Node is visible.

items.subtitle: Runtime expression safety
items.contents:
Runtime expression safety

ScriptNode runtime expressions are evaluated against the engine-provided ctx and Math values. Browser/DOM escape paths are rejected before evaluation.

The safety filter blocks direct references to browser globals such as document, window, globalThis, self, parent, and top; DOM insertion APIs; dynamic code execution such as eval() and Function(); timer APIs; fetch(); XMLHttpRequest; WebSocket; MutationObserver; and Worker.

Use ScriptNode Actions and Controls for engine behavior instead of trying to modify the editor page or exported HTML from a normal runtime expression.

items.subtitle: Numbers and arithmetic
items.contents:
Numbers and arithmetic

Use normal arithmetic in expressions: + add, - subtract, * multiply, / divide, and % get the remainder.

ctx.local.speed * 2
ctx.global.score + 10
ctx.velocity.velocityX / 60

items.subtitle: Comparisons
items.contents:
Comparisons

Comparisons produce true or false.

ctx.local.health > 0
ctx.global.score >= 100
ctx.local.state === "ready"
ctx.local.state !== "dead"

items.subtitle: Logical operators
items.contents:
Logical operators

&& means AND, || means OR, and ! means NOT.

ctx.local.health > 0 && ctx.global.score > 100
ctx.local.state === "win" || ctx.local.state === "draw"
!ctx.local.dead

items.subtitle: Ternary
items.contents:
Ternary

Choose between two values:

condition ? truth : falsy
ctx.local.health > 0 ? "Alive" : "Dead"

items.subtitle: Optional chaining
items.contents:
Optional chaining

?. safely reads through a value that might be missing.

ctx.node?.name
ctx.node?.sprite?.src

items.subtitle: Nullish fallback
items.contents:
Nullish fallback

?? uses the value on the left unless it is null or undefined.

ctx.local.name ?? "Player"

items.subtitle: Property access
items.contents:
Property access

Use . to access named properties.

ctx.position.x
ctx.scale.y
ctx.global.score

items.subtitle: Bracket access
items.contents:
Bracket access

Use brackets when a property name needs to be written as a string.

ctx.events.key["1"]
ctx.local["player-name"]

items.subtitle: Parentheses
items.contents:
Parentheses

Use parentheses to control the order of a calculation and make complex expressions easier to read.

(ctx.global.score + 10) * 2

items.subtitle: Combining syntax
items.contents:
Combining syntax

These pieces can be combined into one expression.

ctx.node?.name === "Player" && (ctx.global.score >= 100 ? true : false)

Build complex expressions from small understandable pieces and test them in the input where they will be used.

items.subtitle: Playing audio
items.contents:
Playing audio

Use the audio controls or the playAudio ScriptNode to play an Audio or MIDI asset during runtime.

items.subtitle: Audio options
items.contents:
Audio options

playAudio supports volume (0–100), start position, duration, looping, fade-in, and fade-out. Decoded Audio data can be cached for lower-latency repeated playback.

Open playAudio

items.subtitle: Stopping audio
items.contents:
Stopping audio

Use the available stop control or the stopAudio ScriptNode to stop active playback.

items.subtitle: Audio preview
items.contents:
Audio preview

Click an Audio asset in the Audio section to open an Audio Preview modal. Use the audio controls there to play and test the sound before using it with playAudio.

The preview does not change the asset or create a game object.

items.subtitle: Stereo panning
items.contents:
Stereo panning

panValue controls left-to-right stereo position and is clamped to -1 through 1.

  • -1 = fully left
  • 0 = center
  • 1 = fully right

The runtime uses a stereo panner when Web Audio is available.

items.subtitle: MIDI Editor overview
items.contents:
MIDI Editor

The MIDI Editor is a piano-roll editor for creating and editing MIDI music. You can draw, erase, move, resize, select, copy, paste, duplicate, and delete notes.

items.subtitle: MIDI name
items.contents:
Changing the MIDI name

The MIDI name is shown beside MIDI Editor. Double-click the name to edit it directly. Press Enter or click elsewhere to save the new name.

items.subtitle: Cancel
items.contents:
Cancel

Canceling the MIDI Editor asks for confirmation before leaving, so you have a chance to avoid losing the current editing session.

items.subtitle: Tracks
items.contents:
Tracks

A MIDI file can contain multiple tracks. Select a track to edit its notes and use the track controls to add or remove tracks where available.

items.subtitle: Notes
items.contents:
Notes

A note has a pitch, time position, duration, and velocity. Notes can be drawn, moved, resized, copied, duplicated, and deleted.

items.subtitle: Note selection
items.contents:
Note selection

Use click selection and marquee selection to select multiple notes. Ctrl/Cmd-click can add or remove individual notes, and Shift can select ranges where supported.

items.subtitle: Snap and length
items.contents:
Snap and length

Snap sets the timing grid used for note placement and movement. Length controls the note timing length used by the editor.

items.subtitle: BPM
items.contents:
BPM

BPM controls playback tempo.

items.subtitle: Playback and loop
items.contents:
Playback and loop

Use Play, Stop, Rewind, and Loop to preview the MIDI while editing.

items.subtitle: MIDI loading progress
items.contents:
MIDI loading progress

When a MIDI file is being edited or loaded, the editor shows a loading progress bar with a percentage. This makes it clear that a large MIDI file is still being processed.

items.subtitle: Import and Export
items.contents:
Import and Export

Import loads a MIDI file into the editor. Export writes the edited MIDI sequence back to a MIDI file.

items.subtitle: Changing the MIDI name
items.contents:
Changing the MIDI name

The MIDI name is shown beside MIDI Editor.

  1. Double-click the name.
  2. The normal text becomes directly editable.
  3. Type the new name.
  4. Press Enter or click somewhere else to apply it.

The rename changes the project asset name rather than changing the musical notes.

items.subtitle: Cancel editing
items.contents:
Cancel editing

Cancel asks for confirmation before leaving the MIDI Editor. This gives you a chance to stop the cancellation if you changed your mind and want to keep editing.

items.subtitle: Play
items.contents:
Play

Play starts the Preferred Scene using the project settings, scripts, input, camera, physics, audio, and variables.

items.subtitle: Debug
items.contents:
Debug

Debug runs the game while exposing additional inspection information. See Debug Output for related details. See Runtime performance and memory for related details.

When Debug is running, the runtime top bar includes an Output button. Open it to see runtime logs, warnings, JavaScript errors, unhandled promise rejections, and ScriptNode execution errors. Output is limited to the most recent 500 entries.

items.subtitle: Runtime changes
items.contents:
Runtime changes

Changes made while the game is running affect the running game state. They are separate from changing the saved project in the editor. Runtime performance

items.subtitle: Scene changes during runtime
items.contents:
Scene changes

A ScriptNode can change the current runtime Scene using loadScene.

items.subtitle: Runtime performance and memory
items.contents:
Runtime performance and memory

Node2D keeps runtime lookup tables for Nodes, Physics bodies, ScriptNodes, connections, event lists, render order, timers, and AI state so common runtime operations do not repeatedly walk the full Scene. See Runtime object lifecycle for related details. See CPU and GPU for related details. See Large scenes for related details.

Rendering keeps a cached draw order and skips Nodes outside the camera area. Physics uses a broadphase before detailed collision tests and adapts substeps for larger Physics populations.

Create Object queues new-object onLoad work instead of executing a large spawn burst synchronously. Destroy Object removes the runtime references needed by the engine so destroyed objects can become garbage-collectable.

items.subtitle: Runtime object lifecycle
items.contents:
Runtime object lifecycle

Created runtime copies receive their own Node ID, numeric ID, ScriptNode IDs, ScriptNode connections, local variables, bodies, render entries, and event registrations. See Create Object for related details.

Destroy Object removes those runtime registrations, removes pending timers and collision pairs, clears target references, and removes the object from its runtime Scene container.

Memory is actually reclaimed by the browser’s JavaScript garbage collector after no reachable references remain.

items.subtitle: CPU and GPU
items.contents:
CPU and GPU

JavaScript, ScriptNodes, and Physics execute on the CPU. Runtime Canvas 2D rendering is requested with browser-friendly low-latency settings, and the browser may hardware-accelerate Canvas rendering using the available GPU.

Node2D does not force a particular GPU; browser, operating system, and device drivers decide the actual rendering path.

items.subtitle: Large scenes
items.contents:
Large scenes

For scenes with many objects, avoid doing expensive work on every onTick when an event can do it instead. Give Physics/Collider components only to objects that need them, destroy temporary objects when finished, and avoid unnecessary DOM/UI work during runtime.

Debug adds Output and variable inspection work, so normal Play mode is lighter when debugging is not needed.

items.subtitle: Debug Output
items.contents:
Debug Output

Click Output in the Debug runtime top bar to open the Output panel.

Messages are grouped as LOG, WARN, or ERROR. ScriptNode exceptions identify the ScriptNode and Node where possible. Use Clear to remove the current Output entries.

Debug captures console log/warn/error calls and browser error/unhandled-rejection events while the Debug runtime is active.

items.subtitle: FPS and Output
items.contents:
Runtime FPS and Output

Play and Debug display a live FPS indicator in the runtime header. Click Output to open the runtime output panel.

Output entries can include LOG, WARN, and ERROR messages. Debug captures console messages plus browser error and unhandled-rejection events while the Debug runtime is active.

items.subtitle: Play versus Debug
items.contents:
Play versus Debug

Play Scene starts the Scene as a game runtime. Debug starts the same runtime with additional debugging facilities such as Output and debug visualization support.

Stop the runtime to return to the editor.

items.subtitle: Particle and object performance
items.contents:
Particle and object performance

Particles are removed automatically after their lifetime. For large games, keep particle counts reasonable, prefer pooling for frequently created objects, hide objects with Visibility when appropriate, and avoid creating temporary objects every frame.

items.subtitle: Particles and Sub Cameras
items.contents:
Particles and Sub Cameras

Runtime Trail particles keep a visible trail until their lifetime ends and do not automatically fade. Sub Cameras render a separate world view into a canvas attached to their Node.

items.subtitle: Consistent Scene variables during onTick
items.contents:
Consistent Scene variables during onTick

During one onTick event dispatch, Node2D gives each participating ScriptNode the same Scene-variable snapshot for that event. A ScriptNode can still write the real Scene variable; that change becomes visible to subsequent runtime work after the current event dispatch rather than causing other onTick Nodes in the same dispatch to observe a different value only because of execution order.

This prevents order-dependent behavior in common multi-Node patterns such as shared positions, scores, spawn values, and synchronized visual markers.

items.contents:
New Project

Creates a fresh project with the normal starting project settings and a starting Scene.

items.subtitle: Save Project
items.contents:
Save Project

Save stores your current project so it can be reopened later.

items.subtitle: Load Project
items.contents:
Load Project

items.contents:
Import NDC

Import NDC loads a complete project file containing your Scenes, Nodes, Components, Scripts, settings, and project assets.

items.subtitle: Export NDC
items.contents:
Export NDC

Export NDC saves the complete project as one portable project file.

items.contents:
Export Project

Export Project creates a playable web package containing the project data, the Node2D runtime package, the shared NDC codec, the engine decoder, and the launcher HTML.

The current standalone layout is index.html, project.ndc, and js/ containing ndcCodec.js, engineDecoder.js, and node2dEngine.ndc, plus optional exported assets, PWA files, and the splash icon.

Use Export NDC when you want editable project data. Use Export Project when you want a playable web package.

items.subtitle: Current project on reload
items.contents:
Current project on reload

Node2D remembers which local project is currently loaded during the browser session. When you reload the page, the editor can automatically reopen that project instead of dropping you back at the project chooser.

This is especially useful when refreshing the page during development. Closing the tab or ending the browser session clears session-only information according to normal browser session storage behavior.

items.subtitle: What is saved in a project
items.contents:
Project contents

Project data includes Scenes and their Nodes, Components, ScriptNodes, connections, Variables, Camera settings, UI components, Game Settings, and imported assets referenced by the project.

Editor-only view state such as viewport pan/zoom is not part of document history.

items.subtitle: Load Local and the Flappy Bird sample
items.contents:
Load Local and the Flappy Bird sample

Load Local lists projects saved on the device. Load Sample Flappy Bird fetches the sample NDC once and saves it into the same Local NDC storage used by normal saved projects.

After it succeeds, Node2D sets flappybirdsample to true in local storage and stops offering the sample loader on that device.

items.subtitle: NDC Import and Export
items.contents:
NDC Import and Export

Exporting and importing .ndc projects uses background workers for the expensive encode/decode work. A progress modal shows the current stage.

During export/import the editor yields between large data chunks so UI events remain responsive. Import asks before replacing an existing project.

items.subtitle: Asset filename uniqueness
items.contents:
Asset filename uniqueness

Sprite, Audio, and MIDI files share one project-wide filename namespace. Two assets cannot keep the same filename, even when they belong to different asset tabs.

When a name is already used, Node2D appends a numeric suffix before the extension: image.png → image (2).png → image (3).png. The check is case-insensitive and applies to imports, generated GIF frames, new Sprite assets, and replacements.

When an existing project is loaded, asset filenames are normalized again so older duplicates are repaired automatically.

items.subtitle: Engine license and game distribution
items.contents:
Engine license and game distribution

The bundled license identifies Node2D Engine as a CardHollow-owned engine under the included non-commercial engine license. The license permits inspection, modification, and non-commercial redistribution of the engine subject to its terms.

The same license explicitly permits commercial games, applications, and other works created with Node2D, and permits distribution of the runtime pieces required as an integrated part of those works. Read the included LICENSE.md for the exact terms and restrictions.

items.subtitle: Export Project
items.contents:
Export Project

Export Project creates a playable web package from the project you are editing. It is meant for sharing or hosting the game, not for continuing to edit the project.

The exported package contains a launcher page, the project data, and the runtime files needed to load the project. Your Scenes, Nodes, Components, ScriptNode graphs, variables, camera/game settings, and project assets are represented in the project data.

The export process reads the current engine files at export time, so a newly exported package uses the runtime build from the editor you exported from.

Typical use

  1. Save the project.
  2. Choose Export Project.
  3. Wait for the export progress to finish.
  4. Open the resulting web package from a web-capable location.
  5. Test the exported game separately from the editor.

Use NDC export when you want the editable project data. Use Project Export when you want a playable web build.

items.subtitle: PWA export and offline use
items.contents:
PWA export and offline use

A PWA-capable export includes the information a browser needs to treat the exported game as an installable web application when the browser and hosting environment support it.

Offline caching lets the browser keep a local copy of the web app so the exported game can continue to open without downloading the same files again while offline.

items.subtitle: Protected engine package
items.contents:
Protected engine package

The exported engine is stored as js/node2dEngine.ndc instead of being copied to many separate readable JavaScript files.

The package uses the same ndcCodec.js as project NDC data. Inside the encoded engine document, each runtime file is represented by a <node2DEngine file="..." length="..."> block containing that file’s source and a matching closing tag.

engineDecoder.js fetches the engine NDC, asks ndcCodec.js to decode it, reconstructs the individual runtime files, and injects them as real JavaScript <script> elements before the exported launcher loads project.ndc.

The current exported runtime package contains the required Node2D runtime files: node.js, assets.js, scriptNodes.js, uiComponents.js, runtimeEngine.js, app.js, and midiParser.js when the project contains MIDI assets. Editor-only files such as the Sprite Editor and Project Exporter are not placed inside the engine package.

items.subtitle: Export splash
items.contents:
Export splash

The Export Project dialog includes a Splash checkbox, enabled by default. You can choose a Sprite asset for Icon and enter the Title shown below it.

If the splash is enabled but no Sprite icon is selected, the exporter falls back to the built-in Node2D icon.svg. The splash is displayed by the exported index.html and is hidden after the runtime has started successfully.

items.subtitle: Exported file layout
items.contents:
Exported file layout

index.html
project.ndc
js/
  ndcCodec.js
  engineDecoder.js
  node2dEngine.ndc

Optional files include exported splash/PWA icons, manifest.json, and sw.js when PWA export is enabled.

items.subtitle: node2dEngine.ndc container
items.contents:
node2dEngine.ndc container

The engine package is itself stored through the existing NDC codec. Its decoded engine payload is a sequence of <node2DEngine> blocks. Each block records the original runtime file path and source length so the decoder can reconstruct the files without using HTML script parsing as the container format.

items.subtitle: engineDecoder.js loading sequence
items.contents:
engineDecoder.js loading sequence

  1. index.html loads ndcCodec.js.
  2. index.html loads engineDecoder.js.
  3. The decoder fetches js/node2dEngine.ndc.
  4. The decoder asks ndcCodec.js to decode the engine package.
  5. The decoder reconstructs the runtime files in package order and injects each as a JavaScript <script> element.
  6. The launcher fetches and loads project.ndc and starts the runtime.

items.subtitle: Engine package scope
items.contents:
Engine package scope

The current export compiler packages node.js, assets.js, scriptNodes.js, uiComponents.js, runtimeEngine.js, app.js, and, when MIDI assets are present, midiParser.js. Editor-only tooling such as Sprite Editor and Project Exporter code is not shipped as part of the protected runtime package.

items.subtitle: Editor Settings
items.contents:
Editor Settings

Editor Settings control how the editor behaves on this device. These preferences are stored locally and are separate from the project.

Available settings include Move / Scale Snap, Rotate Snap, Scale Gizmo, Multiselection Unified Editing, Create New Missing Component, and Auto Save options.

items.subtitle: Shortcut preference storage
items.contents:
Shortcut preferences

Your chosen editor shortcuts are saved locally on your device, so the editor can reuse them after you close and reopen it.

items.subtitle: Download Preferences
items.contents:
Download Preferences

Download Pref... saves your editor preferences as JSON.

The export includes the stored editor preference data rather than only a manually selected list. This allows preferences introduced by a future editor version to travel with the downloaded settings when they are stored in the preference data.

Your chosen keyboard shortcuts, Move / Scale Snap, Rotate Snap, Auto Save, and Auto Save Interval are included when they are stored as editor preferences.

items.subtitle: Move / Scale Snap
items.contents:
Move / Scale Snap

Sets the fixed editing interval used by Node movement and scaling.

Default: 1.

Examples:

  • 1 → values move/scale in whole-unit steps.
  • 0.5 → values use half-unit steps.
  • 0.1 → values use one-tenth-unit steps.
  • 0 → no movement/scale snapping.

The setting is saved with your editor preferences.

items.subtitle: Rotate Snap
items.contents:
Rotate Snap

Sets the fixed angle interval used by the Rotate gizmo.

0° (Off) allows free rotation. A value such as 90° makes the rotation land on right-angle increments.

Rotation snapping is independent from Move / Scale Snap.

items.subtitle: Auto Save
items.contents:
Auto Save

Enable Auto Save when you want Node2D to periodically save the currently loaded project instead of relying only on manual saves.

Auto Save applies to the loaded project. It does not replace exporting a project when you need a portable file.

items.subtitle: Auto Save Interval
items.contents:
Auto Save Interval

This controls how often Auto Save runs, in seconds.

For example, 30 s means the current project is automatically saved about every 30 seconds while Auto Save is enabled.

Set a shorter interval when you are doing frequent small edits. Use a longer interval when you are making large groups of changes.

items.subtitle: Prevent accidental reload or close
items.contents:
Prevent accidental reload or close

When a project is loaded, the editor prevents common accidental reload shortcuts such as F5 and Ctrl/Cmd+R and asks the browser for confirmation when the page is being reloaded or closed.

items.subtitle: Reset Defaults
items.contents:
Reset Defaults

Reset Defaults restores the editor settings to their default values and restores the default keyboard shortcuts. The current editor preference values are replaced by the defaults.

items.subtitle: Import Preferences
items.contents:
Import Preferences

Import Pref... loads an editor preference JSON file previously downloaded from Node2D. Stored editor settings and saved shortcut choices are restored from the file, so the editor changes to match the imported preferences.

The import can also restore stored preference keys contained in the exported preference data, allowing newer preference values to be carried between editor versions.

items.subtitle: Multiselection Unified Editing
items.contents:
Multiselection Unified Editing

Multiselection Unified Editing is enabled by default. When it is on, multiple selected Nodes behave like one group for Move, Scale, and Rotate. Their relative layout is kept while the group is transformed.

When it is off, each selected Node keeps its own transform behavior for Scale and Rotate instead of using one unified group transform.

The Move and Scale gizmos keep their X/Y controls when several Nodes are selected. The Scale Gizmo setting chooses between the Move-style box pointers (Arrow) and the full box-handle version (Full).

items.subtitle: Create New Missing Component
items.contents:
Create New Missing Component

Default: False.

When enabled, a multi-selection edit can create the edited Component on Nodes that do not currently have it. This is useful when you want a group of Nodes to end up with the same Component property even if some Nodes started without that Component.

items.subtitle: Save without blocking the editor
items.contents:
Saving and editor responsiveness

Project saving is queued so repeated Save requests do not overlap. Project encoding is moved to a background Web Worker when supported, while the browser continues handling the editor UI. A newer save request waits as one queued operation instead of starting several saves at once.

Auto Save uses the same queued save path.

items.subtitle: Inspector numeric editing
items.contents:
Inspector value editing

String and numeric Component values use normal inputs. Double-clicking or double-tapping a Component property is not required.

In multi-selection, the same normal inputs participate in MUE and per-field <> state. Editing one field writes that field to every selected Node without changing unrelated fields.

items.subtitle: Component Value Editing
items.contents:
Component Value Editing

Component string and numeric properties are edited directly through their normal inputs. Double-click and double-tap are not part of the Component property editing model.

In multi-selection, these same inputs participate in per-field <> mixed values and MUE propagation. Editing a value commits it to all selected Nodes without changing unrelated properties.

items.subtitle: Scale Gizmo
items.contents:
Scale Gizmo

Arrow is the default. It uses the same screen-relative half-cross style as the Move gizmo: a red X control extends to the right and a green Y control extends upward from the center. The controls use square/box pointers instead of arrowheads.

Full uses the larger box-handle scale gizmo with corner, edge, and side handles.

The setting also applies when several Nodes are selected. With Multiselection Unified Editing enabled, the group is scaled together while keeping the Nodes' relative layout.

items.subtitle: Group and ungroup
items.contents:
Group and Ungroup

Ctrl+G groups the selected Scene items into a new Folder. Ctrl+U moves the children of the selected Folder back into its parent and removes the Folder. Grouping works on top-level selected items from the same parent folder.

items.subtitle: Automatic offline mode
items.contents:
Automatic offline mode

Node2D caches its editor files in your browser whenever you visit it while online.

  • Online: loads the newest editor files and refreshes the browser cache.
  • Offline: opens from the most recently cached editor copy.
  • Online again: requests the newest version and updates the cache when the newer files are available.

The editor cache is separate from Local NDC project storage.

items.subtitle: Offline toast
items.contents:
Offline message

When the editor starts using its saved offline copy, it shows a notification so you know that Offline Mode is active.

items.subtitle: PWA installation
items.contents:
PWA

The editor itself can be used as a Progressive Web App when the browser supports installation. This is separate from exporting a game as a PWA: the editor can also have its own installable/offline behavior.

items.subtitle: Landscape PWA preference
items.contents:
Landscape PWA preference

The Node2D Game Engine PWA manifest requests landscape orientation. On browsers and installed-app environments that support the manifest orientation setting, the installed app prefers to open in landscape.

items.subtitle: Components
items.contents:
Components

Node — object identity. Script — visual script graph. Transform — position, scale, rotation. Text — displayed text. Sprite — image display and animation presentation when its Type is Animation. Animation Sprite — animation frame data used by a Sprite. Physics — physical movement. Collider — collision shape. Progress Bar — value meter. Joystick — touch control.

items.subtitle: Events
items.contents:
Events

onLoad, onTick, onKeybind, onTouch, onMouse, onScreenInput, onJoystick, onAudioPickup, onInputFocus, onInputBlur, onInputChange, onConnectionChange, onCollideWith, and onUnload.

onInputChange sends its out signal when an Input component's text changes while the game is running.

items.subtitle: Actions
items.contents:
Actions

loadScene, stopAnimation, startAnimation, stepAnimation, setVariable, saveVariable, loadVariable, setTransform, setNode, setText, setSprite, setInputComponent, focusInput, blurInput, setPhysics, setCollider, setProgressBar, Follow Object, Chase, Avoid, Destroy Object, Create Object, setVelocity, setCamera, playAudio, startSpeechRecognition, stopSpeechRecognition, stopAudio, clearAudio.

items.subtitle: Controls
items.contents:
Controls

Boolean · Interval · Timeout · isCollidedWith

Control nodes use next to continue a flow where applicable.

items.subtitle: New Event: onConnectionChange
items.contents:
onConnectionChange

onConnectionChange is an Event ScriptNode with a Connection selector containing Online and Offline. It sends out when the browser changes network connection state while the game is running.

items.subtitle: Editor Snap
items.contents:
Editor Snap

Default Move / Scale Snap: 1. Default Rotate Snap: 0° (Off). Both settings can be changed in Editor Settings and are saved on your device.

items.subtitle: Audio playback inputs
items.contents:
Audio playback inputs

playAudio uses src, volume, start, duration, loop, fadein, and fadeout. Volume is a 0–100 value. Frequently played short sounds are decoded and cached so later calls can be scheduled with very little playback overhead.

items.subtitle: New microphone ScriptNodes
items.contents:
Microphone ScriptNodes

Events: onAudioPickup. Actions: startSpeechRecognition and stopSpeechRecognition. These require Use Mic to be enabled in Game Settings.

items.subtitle: Requirements
items.contents:
ScriptNode requirements

A ScriptNode can require a Game Settings feature. Required ScriptNodes remain visible but are disabled until the required feature is enabled.

items.subtitle: Multi-selection editing
items.contents:
Multi-selection editing

Select multiple Nodes and edit them through the group gizmo. Multiselection Unified Editing controls whether transforms are unified or per-Node. Context menus contains Select All - <Name>.

items.subtitle: Scene State ScriptNodes
items.contents:
Scene State ScriptNodes

saveState and loadState store and restore complete runtime Scene snapshots. removeState deletes one named snapshot and clearState deletes all saved snapshots for the current play session. Snapshots survive Scene changes and Scene reloads until removed or the play session ends.

items.subtitle: Node ordering
items.contents:
Node ordering

Index and Move Up/Down

items.subtitle: Visibility and Particles
items.contents:
Visibility and Particles

setVisible shows/hides a Node without destroying it. isVisible checks that state. createParticles creates Circle, Trail, Box, or Sprite particles with position, scale, velocity, acceleration, angle, color, opacity, lifetime, and count.

items.subtitle: Expression timing helpers
items.contents:
Expression timing helpers

Use performance.now() for elapsed-time/profiling measurements and Date.now() for a wall-clock Unix timestamp.

items.subtitle: Documentation query behavior
items.contents:
Documentation query behavior

Node2D Help is designed so context-menu documentation can open the same documentation surface already used by the Help button. The Help page reads help.json, indexes section titles, subtitles, and HTML contents, and accepts query parameters for navigation.

Query forms

  • ?search=Sprite filters the navigation and selects the first matching topic.
  • ?topic=components--sprite selects a specific topic ID.

For a context menu entry such as ? Documentation, the useful target is the exact Node, Component, or ScriptNode name so the Help search can locate the corresponding topic.

items.subtitle: Documentation structure
items.contents:
Documentation structure

Every documentation topic uses the same structure: a section title, a subtitle used in the navigation, an HTML contents body, and a stable id. This keeps the Help renderer predictable and makes direct links possible.

Component and ScriptNode topics should use their exact editor-facing names in the subtitle whenever possible so context-menu queries can find them without requiring aliases.

items.subtitle: A variable name was rejected
items.contents:
Variable name rejected

Choose a name that is not already used in a conflicting scope. The editor keeps the last valid name and shows the field with red error styling when a conflict is detected.

items.subtitle: An asset was rejected
items.contents:
Asset rejected

Check that the file is a supported image or audio type for the drop/import area you are using. Unsupported file types are intentionally rejected.

items.subtitle: The game view does not fit the screen
items.contents:
Game view fitting

Check Game Settings → Screen Type. Windowboxing keeps the 16:9 shape, Stretch fills the screen, Crop fills the screen while cutting edges, and Smart Camera changes the visible camera area.

items.subtitle: A MIDI file is still loading
items.contents:
MIDI loading

Large MIDI files can take time to process. Watch the loading percentage shown by the MIDI Editor instead of assuming the editor is frozen.

items.subtitle: The editor is too narrow
items.contents:
Editor too narrow

Rotate the device or expand the window when the editor displays the small-screen warning. Editing is intentionally blocked while the screen is too narrow.

items.subtitle: Objects move by tiny decimal amounts
items.contents:
Objects move by tiny decimal amounts

Check Editor Settings → Move / Scale Snap. A value such as 0.1 makes the position and scale use tenth-unit steps while the gizmo is dragged.

Snapping is applied to the Move gizmo center/axes and to the Scale gizmo handles. Rotation has its own separate snap setting.

items.subtitle: Scale corner does not keep the ratio
items.contents:
Scale corner behavior

Use a corner handle when you want a proportional resize. Corner handles preserve the starting width-to-height ratio. Use a side handle when you intentionally want to change only width or only height.

items.subtitle: ScriptNode placement
items.contents:
ScriptNode placement

When adding a ScriptNode from the library, Node2D places it at the center of the currently visible Script canvas, taking the current pan and zoom into account. Dragging a ScriptNode into the canvas places it at the actual drop location.

items.subtitle: Mixed-value control does not commit
items.contents:
Multi-selection value will not commit

Press Enter or click/focus outside the control. Changing selection also forces the active edit to commit before the inspector is rebuilt. If values differ, first click <> to activate the normal field; the field starts from the first selected Node and then applies the committed value to the current selection.

items.subtitle: Physics collision participation
items.contents:
Physics isCollider

Collider controls whether the Node has a detectable collision shape. Turning Collider off disables that shape for collision detection.

Physics → isCollider controls whether this Physics body participates in physical collision response. Turning isCollider off does not remove or disable the Collider shape, and the body continues to receive normal physics motion such as gravity, velocity and rotation.

For physical response between two Physics bodies, both bodies must have isCollider enabled. A Collider shape can still be detected/overlapped when isCollider is disabled.

items.subtitle: Multi-selection component editing
items.contents:
Multi-selection component editing

The multi-selection inspector uses the same property-editing model as single selection. Properties are identified by component/property paths rather than a fixed component list.

Mixed values are evaluated independently. For vectors, each axis has its own <> state, so X can be mixed while Y is identical. Editing a mixed property propagates that property to every selected Node.

Adding a component applies to every selected Node that is missing it. Removing a removable component applies to every selected Node that has it. Pasting a component also applies to every selected Node.

items.subtitle: Joint inspector, MUE, and visualization
items.contents:
Joint inspector, MUE, and visualization

Every supported joint property uses the same multi-selection property system as other components. Joint vector axes and scalar values can show their own <> markers.

Joint editor visualization shows connection lines, anchors, type labels, wheel/prismatic axes, and pulley ground guides. Editing a joint does not move bodies in the editor. Runtime physics enforces the actual constraint when the project runs.

items.subtitle: Circle and Triangle collision shapes
items.contents:
Circle and Triangle collision shapes

Circle, Triangle, and Rectangle Collider shapes use the runtime collision pipeline. Circle-versus-polygon detection includes polygon axes plus a closest-feature axis so edge and corner contacts resolve consistently.

Physical collision response requires both Physics bodies to have isCollider enabled. The Collider shape remains available independently of isCollider, so overlap/detection does not erase the configured shape.

Friction and rotational contact response use the same contact solver for circles, triangles, and rectangles.

items.subtitle: Component context-menu documentation
items.contents:
Component context-menu documentation

The component, Node, and Script context menus include ? Documentation. Selecting it opens the Help page with a targeted search query for that component or feature.

items.subtitle: Show Collider
items.contents:
Show Collider

Editor Settings → Debugging → Show Collider controls collider visualization during Debug Play. When enabled, Debug Play draws the same collider geometry used by the runtime physics system, including rectangles, circles, and triangles.

items.subtitle: Show Joints
items.contents:
Show Joints

Editor Settings → Debugging → Show Joints controls joint visualization during Debug Play. When enabled, Debug Play draws joint links, anchors, axes, pulley ground anchors, and joint labels using the same visual style as the editor joint display.

items.subtitle: Documentation links
items.contents:
Documentation links

Use ? Documentation in an editor context menu to open the Help panel with that subject already searched. It stays inside Node2D instead of opening a new browser tab.

items.subtitle: Offline app icon
items.contents:
Offline app icon

Installed Node2D uses dedicated PNG app icons for the PWA manifest and browser install surfaces. This gives the installed app its Node2D icon instead of relying on a generic browser icon.

The editor also keeps its cached app shell available for offline launches after the Service Worker has cached the editor.
